name: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd
title: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd - 500620 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GE Shipping's Q2 FY27 was its second-highest profit quarter on record, with interim dividend held at INR14.40 and NAV at an all-time high.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as very profitable, slightly below the prior quarter but the second highest in company history. NAV reached an all-time high and the interim dividend was maintained at INR14.40 per share. Crude tanker TCY fell from about USD93,000/day in Q1 to about USD73,000/day in Q2, with Aframaxes dropping from about USD85,000 to USD50,000, while LPG TCY rose from USD41,000 to USD46,000. Spot Suezmax rates have since fallen from USD350,000-400,000/day to USD130,000-150,000/day as Strait of Hormuz traffic resumed, though management said these levels remain well above last year.

segments.name: Crude tankers (Suezmax/Aframax/VLCC)
segments.commentary: Q2 average TCY about USD73,000/day vs USD93,000 in Q1, mainly Aframaxes. Two Suezmaxes fixed on one-year time charters (one owned, one in-chartered), so 50% of the four-Suezmax fleet is fixed through Aug/Sep 2027. Management said spot Suezmax rates have fallen from USD350-400k to USD130-150k/day in the last 10-12 days.

segments.name: Product tankers (MR/LR2)
segments.commentary: Average TCY about USD32,000/day vs USD45,000 in Q1. MR spot about USD50-60k/day with diesel cracks strong; product tanker order book about 22% of fleet. One LR2 (Jag Laxman, 2009-built Jag Lokesh sold in July) fixed on one-year charter.

segments.name: LPG carriers
segments.commentary: Spot rates about USD140,000/day in H1 vs USD55,000 a year earlier. Average TCY rose to USD46,000 from USD41,000 on repricings. Newly acquired VLGC Jag Vikrant (2015-built) carries a fixed charter to about September 2029. LPG order book about 40% of fleet.

segments.name: Dry bulk
segments.commentary: Modest improvement in TCY QoQ. Capesize spot down from about USD40,000 in September to USD30,000-35,000/day. Kamsarmax Jag Amit (2015-built) acquired; a 2019-built Kamsarmax is due for delivery within about a month. Dry bulk order book about 16% of fleet.

segments.name: Offshore (jack-up rigs)
segments.commentary: 19 rigs (4 outside India, 15 in India). Two Indian rigs signed 3-year contracts to FY30, with pricing down about USD25,000-30,000/day from prior contract on one; one rig still needs employment. Eight vessels up for repricing in H2 FY27, four bid into Indian tenders awaiting outcome. Management expects 60-90 days downtime per rig turnaround, a near-term P&L drag.

guidance_outlook: No earnings or revenue guidance given; management said the company does not forecast spot earnings.

Coverage for Q3 FY27 is 58% of crude carrier revenue days as of 1 October; management said coverage is now much higher. Crude and product tanker TCY for the December quarter expected significantly above the prior quarter, though no figure was given.
Offshore run-rate operating EBITDA of about INR1,000 crore p.a. seen as broadly sustainable, but the next couple of quarters could be weak due to rig turnarounds.
Management expects positive fleet growth in calendar 2027.
Share buyback: intention to complete as soon as possible, with a price cap of INR1,530/share. Next buyback cannot begin until 12 months after closure.
Interim dividend maintained at INR14.40/share; management said the company will continue paying dividends.
capex_capacity: Newbuild Suezmax tanker due in a little over two years; a deliberate move to add modern tonnage given high second-hand prices.
Acquired in the last weeks: Jag Amit (2015-built Kamsarmax), Jag Vikrant (2015-built VLGC with charter to about Sept 2029), and a 2019-built Kamsarmax due within about a month.
Sold 2009-built LR2 Jag Lokesh in July and replaced it with the modern LR2 Jag Laxman, now on one-year charter.
Management said it needs to deploy over USD1 billion in ships but is waiting for prices to fall to its target levels before adding more capacity.
Newly acquired foreign-flag ships are registered under the Marshall Islands flag and remain owned and operated from Mumbai; tonnage tax applies.
demand_pricing: Suezmax spot earnings spiked to USD600,000-700,000/day headline, inflated by Hormuz loading and Novorossiysk premium. Excluding these, the peak was about USD350-400k/day around late Sept/early Oct; now about USD130-150k/day, falling USD15-25k/day.
Ship-to-ship shuttle loading out of the Strait of Hormuz adds 8-9 days to a roughly 45-46 day Middle East to Far East VLCC voyage, tightening the market.
Crude order book about 28% of fleet, mostly delivering 2028-2030 (only 7.5% due by end-2027). Product tanker order book about 22%. Scrapping minimal.
Suezmax prices up about 50% QoQ; smaller tankers up 5-20%; bulk carriers up 5-10%.
Time charter rates trade at 60-70% discounts to spot in hot markets, so locking in earnings via long charters is not economic now.
Indian one-year VLGC deal reportedly around USD100,000/day; MGC repricing estimated at USD40-50k/day (unconfirmed).
Ship-prices vs NAV: management said NAV would be about INR250/share lower at January 2026 ship values. Rupee moved from INR95.5 (end Sept) to below INR94/USD.

qa_highlights.question: Why were so few crude and product tankers fixed on longer time charters at the spike?
qa_highlights.answer: Time charter rates were 60-70% below spot (e.g., 2-year Suezmax TC about USD60-70k vs spot USD300k). Only one Suezmax owned and one in-chartered were fixed for one year, 50% of the Suezmax fleet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the newbuild Suezmax a shift toward more tanker capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. Second-hand prices are high and replacement is hard for a year or two; the newbuild is a core modern-vessel purchase at a lower premium. Management said it may not deploy all its capital in second-hand ships even in weak markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of reverting ship values to January 2026 on NAV, and where is ship price going?
qa_highlights.answer: NAV would be about INR250/share lower at January 2026 values. Management has not seen crude tanker transactions in the last two weeks and expects prices to fall significantly, but this is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company do another buyback after completing this one, instead of paying dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: No. A new buyback is barred for 12 months after closure. Management views the buyback as capital allocation (buying its own fleet at a discount), not a dividend substitute, and will keep paying dividends for loyal long-term holders.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to shipping rates if a US-Iran deal ends the disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Rates should fall from current highs but remain firm, since pre-war Suezmax earnings were USD70-80k/day in February and inventories need to rebuild. Sanctions relief would open Iranian cargoes to the legitimate fleet and scrap old shadow-fleet tonnage.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company avoid the high-risk Hormuz and Novorossiysk loading routes?
qa_highlights.answer: The concern is crew safety, not insurance. Management does not want to expose seafarers to drone or missile attack, and has not traded Russian cargoes since February 2022.

qa_highlights.question: How much offshore EBITDA is sustainable and what are the new rig contract rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Run-rate of about INR1,000 crore/year is broadly sustainable, but rig turnarounds of 60-90 days each weigh on the next couple of quarters. One re-contract is about USD25-30k/day lower than the prior rate.

risks_watch: Sharp spot-rate correction as Hormuz shuttle inefficiency unwinds; Suezmax spot already down about 60% from peak per management.
Ship-value declines could offset cash-flow NAV accretion; no crude tanker transactions seen in the last two weeks.
Geopolitical outcome (US-Iran deal terms, sanctions treatment of Iranian oil, Russia-Ukraine) unpredictable; management gives no guidance.
Order book of 28% for crude tankers and 22% for product tankers; limited scrapping in a strong market.
Offshore: eight vessels up for repricing in H2 FY27, four tenders pending; rig downtime 60-90 days each.
Buyback progress (cap INR1,530/share) and possible market volatility.
Quarterly TCY for December quarter: management says tanker TCY will be significantly above Q2 on the September spike, but gave no number.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and cash generation but cautious on the outlook, repeatedly declining to forecast rates, earnings or revenue. Most evasive on rate direction and NAV after the Suezmax correction, which management said is "anybody's guess."
key_quotes: Another very profitable quarter, slightly lower than the previous immediately preceding quarter, but second highest in historical terms.
The NAV is at its highest ever, and the interim dividend has been maintained at the previous quarter's level of INR14.40 per share for this quarter.
The issue is not insurance. Finally, we think about the crew.

We don't forecast. Most of our capacity is on the spot market, and therefore we don't forecast what our earnings could be, and we don't give guidance, because it is not possible for us, unless we are able to forecast the spot market accurately.
We are doing a buyback as a way to buy our own fleet at a discount.
